'''''Tetraclinis''''' (also called arar,<ref>{{cite web
 | title=Tetraclinis articulata
 | work=The Gymnosperm Database
 | url=http://www.conifers.org/cu/Tetraclinis.php
 | access-date=2011-02-13 }}</ref> araar<ref>but it is ambiguous Arabic name also given to ''[[Juniperus phoenicea]]''</ref> or Sictus tree) is a [[genus]] of [[Pinophyta|coniferous]] trees in the cypress family [[Cupressaceae]], containing only one species, '''''Tetraclinis articulata''''', also known as '''Thuja articulata''',<ref name="Memidex">[http://www.memidex.com/sandarac+wood Memidex: sandarac (wood)] Retrieved 2012-05-16</ref> '''sandarac''', '''sandarac tree'''<ref>[http://dictionary.reverso.net/english-definition/sandarac%20tree Collins: sandarac and sandarac tree] Retrieved 2012-05-16</ref> or '''Barbary thuja''',<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=fuwBN04nF9QC&dq=barbary+thuja&pg=PA118 Jacques Blondel & James Aronson: ''Biology and Wildlife of the Mediterranean Region'', Oxford University Press 1999] Retrieved 2012-05-16</ref> [[endemism|endemic]] to the western [[Mediterranean region]], particularly in [[southern Europe]] and [[North Africa]].

== Distribution and habitat ==
It is native to northwestern [[Africa]] in the [[Atlas Mountains]] of [[Morocco]], [[Algeria]], and [[Tunisia]], with two small outlying populations on [[Malta]], and near [[Cartagena, Spain|Cartagena]] in southeast [[Spain]] in [[Europe]]. It grows at relatively low altitudes in a hot, dry [[Subtropics|subtropical]] [[Mediterranean climate]].<ref name="farjon">Farjon, A. (2005). ''Monograph of Cupressaceae and Sciadopitys''. Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew. {{ISBN|1-84246-068-4}}</ref>
The species has reportedly become an [[invasive species]] in the eastern Mediterranean drylands.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cohen |first1=O. |last2=Sheffer |first2=E. |last3=Bar-Shmuel |first3=N. |last4=Weber |first4=G. |last5=Guy |first5=A. |last6=Avioz |first6=T. |last7=Osem |first7=Y. |title=Determinants of naturalization and invasion of ''Tetraclinis articulata'' in eastern Mediterranean drylands: Is it a "superinvader"? |journal=Biol. Invasions |date=2025 |volume=27 |issue=3 |article-number=94 |doi=10.1007/s10530-025-03538-z|bibcode=2025BiInv..27...94C |doi-access=free }}</ref> The genus once had a much broader range during the [[Oligocene]]–[[Miocene]], with some species occurring in [[North America]].<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Cones, Seeds, and Foliage of Tetraclinis salicornioides (Cupressaceae) from the Oligocene and Miocene of Western North America: A Geographic Extension of the European Tertiary Species|url=https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/10.1086/314245|journal=International Journal of Plant Sciences|date=2000|issn=1058-5893|pages=331–344|volume=161|issue=2|doi=10.1086/314245|first=Zlatko|last=Kvaček|first2=Steven R.|last2=Manchester|first3=Howard E.|last3=Schorn|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
== Taxonomy ==
Its closest relatives are ''[[Platycladus]], [[Microbiota (plant)|Microbiota]]'', and ''[[Calocedrus]]'', with the closest resemblance to the latter. In older texts, it was sometimes treated in ''[[Thuja]]'' or ''[[Callitris]]'', but it is less closely related to those genera.<ref name=farjon/>

== Description ==
[[File:Alhucemas (11).JPG|300px|thumb|''Tetraclinis'' cones at [[Al Hoceima National Park]]]]

It is a small, slow-growing tree, to 6–15 m (rarely 20 m) tall and 0.5 m (rarely 1 m) trunk diameter, often with two or more trunks from the base. The foliage forms in open sprays with scale-like [[leaf|leaves]] 1–8 mm long and 1–1.5 mm broad; the leaves are arranged in opposite decussate pairs, with the successive pairs closely then distantly spaced, so forming apparent whorls of four. The [[conifer cone|cones]] are 10–15 mm long, green ripening brown in about 8 months from pollination, and have four thick scales arranged in two opposite pairs. The [[seed]]s are 5–7 mm long and 2 mm broad, with a 3–4 mm broad papery wing on each side.<ref name=farjon/><ref name=rushforth>Rushforth, K. (1999). ''Trees of Britain and Europe''. Collins {{ISBN|0-00-220013-9}}.</ref>

It is one of only a small number of conifers able to [[coppice]] (regrow by sprouting from stumps), an adaptation to survive [[wildfire]] and moderate levels of browsing by animals. Old trees that have sprouted repeatedly over a long period form large burls at the base, known as ''lupias''.<ref name=farjon/>

==Uses and symbolism==
It is the [[national tree]] of [[Malta]], where it is known as ''għargħar'' (derived from the Arabic {{lang|ar|عَرْعَر}} {{Transliteration|ar|ʿarʿar}}). It is now being used locally in afforestation projects.{{citation needed|date=March 2023}}

The [[resin]], known as [[sandarac]], is used to make [[varnish]] and [[lacquer]]; it is particularly valued for preserving [[painting]]s.

The [[wood]], known as  thuya wood,<ref>[http://www.arc-genesis.co.uk/html/thuya_wood.html Arc-genesis: Thuya Wood] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110808080529/http://www.arc-genesis.co.uk/html/thuya_wood.html |date=2011-08-08 }} Retrieved 2012-05-16</ref> citron wood,<ref name="Memidex"/> and alerce,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/alerce|title = Definition of ALERCE}}</ref> and historically also known as [[thyine wood]], is used for decorative woodwork, particularly wood from burls at the base of the trunk. It has been used thus since antiquity ({{langx|grc|θύον}},<ref>{{cite dictionary |url=https://logeion.uchicago.edu/%CE%B8%CF%8D%CE%BF%CE%BD |author=[[Liddell & Scott]] |dictionary=A Greek-English Lexicon |title=θύον |via=[[Logeion]] }}</ref><ref>{{cite dictionary |first=Robert S. P. |last=Beekes |dictionary=[[Indo-European Etymological Dictionary|Etymological Dictionary of Greek]] |title=θύον |page=565 |year=2009 |publisher=Brill }}</ref> {{langx|la|citrus}}<ref>{{cite dictionary |url=https://archive.org/details/m-de-vaan-2008-etymological-dictionary-of-latin-and-the-other-italic-languages/page/116/mode/2up |dictionary=[[Indo-European Etymological Dictionary|Etymological Dictionary of Latin and the other Italic Languages]] |year=2008 |publisher=Brill |first=Michiel |last=de Vaan |title=citrus |page=116 }}</ref>), and was used to make valuable furniture in the time of the [[Roman Empire]].<ref>{{cite dictionary |url=https://logeion.uchicago.edu/citrus |author=Lewis & Short |dictionary=[[A Latin Dictionary]] |title=citrus |via=[[Logeion]]}}</ref> The market in Morocco is unsustainable, focusing as it does on the burl, and has resulted in mass deforestation of the species. The species is also threatened by [[overgrazing]], which can kill the coppice regrowth before it gets tall enough to be out of the reach of livestock.<ref name=farjon/>

===Cultivation===
The species is cultivated to be grown as an [[ornamental tree]], valued in hot, dry climates. It is also pruned in a [[hedge (barrier)|hedge]] form, for privacy and security.<ref name=rushforth/> The plant can be trained for use as [[bonsai]] specimens.

==Fossil record==
A related [[Extinction|extinct]] species, ''Tetraclinis salicornioides,'' has leaf and cone [[fossil]]s of [[Messinian]] age (ca. 5.7 Ma) that have been uncovered in Monte Tondo and [[Borgo Tossignano]], northern [[Apennines]], [[Italy]].<ref>Palaeoenvironmental analysis of the Messinian macrofossil floras of Tossignano and Monte Tondo (Vena del Gesso Basin, Romagna Apennines, northern Italy) - Vasilis Teodoridis, Zlatko Kvacek, Marco Sami and Edoardo Martinetto - December 2015 DOI: 10.14446/AMNP.2015.249.</ref>
